transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-08
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Theo Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood Security), Evan Brooks (Halcyon Head of Platform), Sana Iqbal (Halcyon Security Architect), Liam O'Connor (Halcyon IdAM)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be imperfect):
- Walkthrough of SAML SSO flows and preferences (IdP-initiated prioritized)
- SCIM provisioning: discuss delta syncs and rate limits; plan for test tenant
- RBAC: propose tenant/org/team roles, least-privilege mapping, and service account pattern
- Audit logs: events to surface, retention policy, and secure export
- Encryption/KMS: per-tenant keys vs shared key, rotation cadence, HSM/KMS integration

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. I'll do a quick intro, I'm Maya, I'm the AE on the account, joining from Redwood, and theo will walk through the technical patterns. Priya is here for security questions.
[00:12] Evan Brooks: Thanks, Maya. Happy to be here — we want to nail the identity flow before we spin up anything in prod.
[00:18] Theo Alvarez: Cool, yeah, I'll share my screen in a sec. High level agenda, SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, RBAC matrix, logs and encryption. If at any point you want to deep-dive, stop me.
[00:30] Sana Iqbal: Quick note — Halcyon must keep PII in EU regions for this pilot, so data residency is a blocker unless we figure out where logs and keys live.
[00:40] Theo Alvarez: Understood. We'll cover EU tenancy and key residency. Just to level-set: Redwood supports both SP-initiated and IdP-initiated SAML flows; most teams prefer IdP-initiated for corporate SSO because the IdP controls session lifetime.
[00:54] Liam O'Connor: For us, IdP-initiated is preferable. Also, for provisioning, we want event-driven delta provisioning rather than full weekly syncs. Minimize blast radius.
[01:06] Theo Alvarez: Yes, we support delta SCIM operations (PATCH) and full sync. There's a rate-limit surface — default 100 reqs/min per tenant — we can adjust for Dedicated customers but on hosted tiers that's our baseline.
[01:26] Evan Brooks: 100 reqs/min is fine for our size. Two questions: 1) How do you map SCIM groups to RBAC roles? 2) How do you handle service accounts for CI pipelines that need elevated rights?
[01:40] Priya Nair: I'll take the RBAC part. Recommended pattern is narrow, composable roles: admin/org-admin, team-maintainer, read-only, and per-service service-account roles. Avoid giving service accounts broad org-admin scopes.
[01:55] Sana Iqbal: We're concerned about privilege escalation if someone can create a service account and then give it broader rights. Any approval/workflow for that?
[02:04] Theo Alvarez: Nowadays customers do two things: require SAML group->role mapping enforced via SCIM, plus an out-of-band approval workflow for granting org-admins. Redwood's Console logs service-account creation events and you can gate creation behind 2-step verification or require an approval rule via our API.
[02:22] Liam O'Connor: Are those events exportable? We need to push to our SIEM.
[02:27] Theo Alvarez: Yes, audit events can be exported to syslog/CloudWatch/Splunk via our export endpoint. We include event types: user.login, saml.assertion, scim.create, scim.patch, key.rotation, service_account.create, role.grant, role.revoke, model.deploy, etc.
[02:50] Evan Brooks: Retention — how long are logs kept by default? Our compliance needs seven years for access logs.
[02:58] Priya Nair: Default retention is 90 days on hosted. For Dedicated and Private you can configure long-term retention or push logs to your storage. For seven years we'd recommend exporting to your SIEM or object storage with lifecycle rules.
[03:12] Sana Iqbal: Ok. Encryption — do you support customer-managed keys (CMK) for data at rest? We need keys that we can rotate and revoke per-tenant.
[03:22] Theo Alvarez: Yes. We support KMS integrations: AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and third-party HSMs via our KMS bridge. Two patterns: shared platform key with envelope encryption, or per-tenant CMK. Per-tenant CMK is available for Dedicated and Private deployments.
[03:39] Evan Brooks: What's key rotation look like? We need zero-downtime key rotation and a retained rewrap window.
[03:46] Theo Alvarez: We rotate by creating a new key version and re-wrapping the data keys in the background. For large datasets we do lazy rewrap on read, plus a background job. Retention/roll-back window configurable; default 30 days.
[03:59] Liam O'Connor: Slight transcription note, earlier you said KV cache — that was actually "KV cache" right? I want to make sure it's not being turned into "K V cash" in any of the docs.
[04:08] Maya Chen: Haha, yep, we'll ensure docs use the right terms. Sometimes the auto-transcribe mangles that.
[04:15] Sana Iqbal: Back to SCIM — do you support SCIM deltas with 'bulk' for initial sync and then PATCH for updates?
[04:23] Theo Alvarez: Yes, recommended pattern: initial bulk full-sync (POST list) then switch to incremental PATCH delta endpoint. We'll provide the exact sample payloads. Also note our SCIM supports group membership changes with "members" edits and optional provisioning filters.
[04:40] Evan Brooks: For RBAC mapping, we have org->team->project hierarchy. Can Redwood handle role inheritance? e.g., org-admin implicitly has team-admin across teams?
[04:50] Priya Nair: We typically model with explicit inheritance rules. Org-admin can be flagged to inherit team-admin. But we advise caution — inheritance increases blast radius. Better to keep high-priv roles narrowly scoped and grant team-admin where required.
[05:06] Liam O'Connor: Can we have time-limited elevated roles? Like admin for 8 hours for a ticket, then auto-revoke?
[05:12] Theo Alvarez: Yep, ephemeral role grants are supported via time-bound tokens and our RBAC API supports grant with expiry. We also integrate with approval workflows for temporary elevation.
[05:24] Evan Brooks: Onboarding flow — would you recommend JIT provisioning versus SCIM?
[05:28] Maya Chen: JIT is simple for SSO-only flows but you lose pre-provisioned permissions and group membership syncing. For most enterprise customers we recommend SCIM for deterministic role mapping.
[05:38] Sana Iqbal: Could we do a hybrid? SCIM for groups and base roles, and JIT to seed ad-hoc accounts?
[05:45] Theo Alvarez: Absolutely, hybrid is common — SCIM for directory and group authoritative mapping, JIT for occasional contractors who sign in via SAML but shouldn't be in SCIM source-of-truth.
[05:55] Evan Brooks: Let's talk compliance docs. Maya, can you share SOC2, ISO scopes and a redacted audit log sample?
[06:01] Maya Chen: Yes, I'll share SOC2 Type II and our ISO27001 scope summary. We can provide a sanitized audit log extract for the patterns we discussed.
[06:09] Sana Iqbal: About data residency — if we enforce EU-only, will keys and logs remain in eu-west? Which components might still touch us-east?
[06:18] Theo Alvarez: With Private or Dedicated we can pin compute, keys and logs to eu-west region. For hosted multi-tenant, metadata may transit outside region for control plane operations but we offer data-processing guarantees and can sign DPA with EU-only processing clauses. We'll include the exact topology in the doc pack.
[06:36] Liam O'Connor: Networking — we'll need specific IP allowlist ranges for SCIM and SAML endpoints so our firewall team can open them.
[06:42] Maya Chen: We'll provide the CIDR list for the sandbox and production endpoints. Also PRs for a static egress for Dedicated.
[06:49] Priya Nair: A couple of security nuances — 1) service accounts should not have personal MFA, instead require key rotation and short-lived tokens, 2) ensure service-account creation events are immutable in audit logs, 3) enforce RBAC change approval for org-admin grants.
[07:08] Theo Alvarez: Noted. Audit logs are append-only and we sign log-shards server-side; exports inherit those protections.
[07:16] Evan Brooks: Any gotchas on SCIM attributes? We saw differences in email vs userName fields and federated IDs across IdPs.
[07:24] Theo Alvarez: Yeah, attribute mapping varies. We'll include a mapping matrix for Okta, Azure AD, Ping, and a generic SAML attribute map. Some IdPs use mail as userName, others use userPrincipalName.
[07:36] Sana Iqbal: For initial POC, we'll give you a test Okta tenant. We prefer Okta but still want to see Azure AD flow.
[07:44] Maya Chen: Great — action items: we'll send SP metadata, SCIM samples, SOC2/ISO docs, and CIDR lists. Let's schedule the sandbox run — two weeks? That matches your timeline?
[07:58] Evan Brooks: Two weeks sounds good. We'll aim to have the test IdP ready by 2026-02-10.
[08:05] Liam O'Connor: Quick question — do you support SCIM filtering, e.g., only sync users in group "product-engineering"?
[08:11] Theo Alvarez: Yes, SCIM supports group filters and scoping rules; we can exclude certain schemas.
[08:18] Sana Iqbal: Anything else re encryption — how are secrets for service accounts stored?
[08:23] Priya Nair: Secrets are stored encrypted with envelope keys; private keys are kept in KMS and we rotate regularly. Access to decrypt is via RBAC-gated service.
[08:34] Evan Brooks: Good. If we wrap this up — recap next steps?
[08:37] Maya Chen: Recap: Redwood to send SAML/SP metadata, SCIM payload samples, SOC2/ISO docs, and CIDR lists. Halcyon to provide test IdP and two service accounts. Schedule sandbox session week of Feb 15. Action items captured in the doc. Any final Qs?
[08:53] Sana Iqbal: None from me. Thanks.
[08:57] Evan Brooks: Thanks all.
[09:00] Maya Chen: Thanks, talk soon.

End of transcript.
